title: World Heart Day 2026 is a reminder to learn the warning signs
dek: September 29 is World Heart Day, and this year's campaign asks people to learn the signs of heart disease and take care of their hearts.
body: Today is World Heart Day. The World Heart Federation's campaign this year is called "Don't Miss a Beat," and it focuses on the signs of heart disease that people often miss until it is too late.

The numbers are sobering. According to the federation, cardiovascular disease is the world's leading killer and claims more than 20 million lives each year. It also says 80 percent of those deaths come from risk factors that can be managed or prevented.

That second number is the one I hold on to. It means a lot of what protects our hearts is ordinary. Moving our bodies, going to regular checkups and paying attention when something feels off can make a real difference.

I am not a doctor, and I do not want to pretend to be one. I just know that it is easy to put off a checkup when life is busy, and it is easy to ignore a symptom because we do not want to make a fuss.
Today, take a short walk if you can, and if you have been putting off a checkup, make the appointment before the day ends.
